title: The letter you never send

body.heading: Say it all, on paper
paragraphs: Some things are too raw, too late or too complicated to say out loud. Writing them as a letter gives them a shape. Address it properly, write honestly, and do not censor yourself; no one is going to read this but you.
People write unsent letters to old friends, to former selves, to people who have died, and to people they will speak to tomorrow but want to face calmly first.

body.heading: Decide what happens to it
paragraphs: When you finish, you have choices: keep it in a private place, reread it once and destroy it, or mine it for a calmer real conversation. All three are legitimate endings.
If the letter reveals something you genuinely need to say, consider a shorter, kinder second version for sending. The unsent letter did the emotional work; the sent one can do the practical work.

takeaway: Write the honest version for yourself first; decide about sending later.
